To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Down syndrome (DS) patients have a high risk of developing acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (ALL); 2) the majority of DS-ALLs carry the ETV6-RUNX1 fusion gene and are associated with a good prognosis; and 3) the presence of the ETV6-NTRK3 fusion gene is associated with a poor prognosis in DS-ALL patients.

the risk of developing acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (ALL) in Down syndrome is 20 times higher compared to non-DS patients and the most common subtype of ALL in DS is B-cell ALL, with the t(9;22) translocation being the most common cytogenetic abnormality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of molecular mechanisms involved in the genesis and progression of Down syndrome acute lymphoblastic leukemias.
the molecular and genetic basis of Down syndrome and the development of novel therapies to improve the health and well-being of people with Down syndrome.

the development of a new approach for the treatment of acute lymphoblastic leukaemia in Down syndrome, which is based on the use of a new drug, the combination of the drug with other drugs, or the combination of different drugs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Down syndrome is a risk factor for acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (ALL) and that ALL in children with Down syndrome is a separate entity with its own unique characteristics, including a high rate of spontaneous remission.

the incidence of ALL in Down syndrome is increased 10 to 30 fold, that ALL in DS is more often of T-cell origin and is associated with a high frequency of T-cell receptor gene rearrangements, that ALL in Down syndrome has a more favorable outcome and is associated with an increased risk of CNS involvement.

acute lymphoblastic leukaemia in Down syndrome is a distinct disease entity with a very good prognosis and with an excellent outcome in most of the cases, even when the disease is not diagnosed and treated according to the current protocols.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the most important risk factor for developing ALL in Down Syndrome is the presence of a constitutional trisomy 21, and the second most important risk factor is the presence of the BCR-ABL1 fusion gene.
the incidence of acute lymphoblastic leukemias is increased 10 to 20-fold in patients with Down syndrome.
we found a high incidence of acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (ALL) in children with Down syndrome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Down syndrome acute leukemia has a unique genetic signature that is distinct from that of other acute leukemias.
there are no specific genetic alterations that are associated with Down syndrome and that the most frequent alterations are those that are also seen in sporadic ALL.
the prognosis of Down syndrome patients with ALL is excellent, and that we should not be afraid to treat them with intensive chemotherapy.
